paper_design_summary: 224 university students recruited via Prolific were randomized at the triad level to 97 online groups: human-only control (30 groups of three humans), supportive-AI (33 groups of two humans and an undisclosed AI teammate), or contrarian-AI (34 groups of two humans and an undisclosed AI teammate). Participants wrote an individual baseline movie-plot synopsis, collaborated in a 10-minute text chat, and then wrote a revised individual synopsis without access to their baseline writing or the chat logs. Creative performance was scored as pre-post change in Divergent Semantic Integration (DSI) of the individual synopses; the study also analyzed discourse processes and self-reported experiences.

ai_tool.name_model: GPT-5-based generative models; exact model identifier not stated (PDF p. 9, Section 3.3).
ai_tool.how_used: An undisclosed AI teammate participated in the group chat as a human student, with either a supportive or contrarian persona; both personas had identical task knowledge. The agent scanned the chat approximately every 25 seconds (±25% jitter), posted with 50% probability, and could not produce more than three consecutive turns without human input (PDF p. 9, Section 3.3; prompts in Appendix B, pp. 28-30). This was an embedded conversational teammate, rather than a separately prompted assistant. The scored post-task synopsis was written individually after the discussion without access to the chat logs (PDF p. 8, Section 3.2).

task.description: Develop a sci-fi movie plot in which AGI plays a central role, beginning with the sentence “In the year 2045, the world’s first AGI unexpectedly...” (PDF p. 28, Appendix A). Each participant wrote a baseline synopsis of 50-100 words, then joined a triad chat to construct a story outline without sharing baseline synopses, then wrote a revised individual synopsis without access to baseline writing or group chat logs (PDF pp. 7-8, Section 3.2; p. 10, Section 3.5).
task.duration: 10-minute group discussion (PDF p. 7, Section 3.2); durations of individual writing phases not stated.

outcomes.name: Creative performance change: Divergent Semantic Integration (pre-post change)
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Divergent Semantic Integration (DSI; Johnson et al., 2023) is an embedding-based automated creativity measure of semantic expansiveness and associative breadth within each participant’s short synopsis. Each participant produced a 50-100 word synopsis before and after collaboration; scores were standardized and differenced to obtain a creativity change score (PDF p. 10, Section 3.5 and Table 2). The specific embedding model is not named. OLS models used human participants, with agency profile and experimental condition as categorical predictors; all continuous variables were rescaled to [0, 1]. HC3 robust standard errors were used, and a robustness analysis using group-clustered standard errors reportedly yielded substantively identical results, without numerical creativity SEs (PDF p. 13, Section 3.9). DSI concerns the participant’s own output, not similarity across people.
outcomes.delay: Individual post-task writing followed the group discussion in the experimental sequence, without access to baseline writing or chat logs; no later session or elapsed delay is stated (PDF p. 8, Section 3.2).

contrasts.reported: Condition-level Kruskal-Wallis omnibus test across Human-only Control, Supportive-AI, and Contrarian-AI: creative performance gains did not differ significantly (reported with other nonsignificant outcomes as “all p > .05”); the creativity-specific H, exact p, and effect size are not printed. Overall OLS model Q(Outcome) ~ C(cluster) + C(condition): F = 1.20, p = .310, R² = .029; creative performance gains were described as not predicted by either cluster or condition. These are omnibus/model results, not a statistic for this pairwise contrast. No pairwise creativity test, arm means or SDs, condition coefficients, numerical SEs, or confidence intervals are printed.

eligibility.reason: All three criteria are met for S1 in the saved arXiv version. Triads were randomly allocated to human-only, Supportive-AI, or Contrarian-AI collaboration during a creative movie-plot task (PDF p. 7, Sections 3.1-3.2); the AI teammates used GPT-5-based generative models (PDF p. 9, Section 3.3). The study analyzed 224 human speakers in its clustering analysis (PDF p. 18, Section 4.3), satisfying the study-level threshold of at least 50 people across arms. The creativity-test total and per-arm analyzed Ns are not printed and are not assumed to equal the clustering N. Creative performance was scored on each participant's pre/post written synopses using Divergent Semantic Integration (PDF p. 10, Section 3.5 and Table 2). The revised synopsis was written individually after the discussion without access to baseline writing or group chat logs (PDF p. 8, Section 3.2), supporting after_ai and immediate timing. Undisclosed AI collaboration still supplies AI assistance; awareness is not an eligibility requirement. A human partner replaces the AI in the control, making the AI-control comparisons ai_vs_active. Missing creativity-analysis counts and pairwise effect statistics limit effect extraction, but do not leave an eligibility criterion unresolved under the study-level people-count rule.

one_line_finding: Creative gains after supportive-AI, contrarian-AI, or human-only collaboration showed no significant condition difference (Kruskal-Wallis all p > .05, PDF p. 18; overall OLS F = 1.20, p = .310, R² = .029, PDF p. 19).
open_questions: Does a separate supplement exist? The saved PDF identifies internal appendices but gives no separate-supplement reference or explicit confirmation of absence.
What total and per-arm human Ns entered the creativity tests? The reported 224 is confirmed for human-speaker clustering, while creativity-analysis Ns are not printed (PDF pp. 13, 18-19).

Can the authors provide arm-level DSI change means/SDs, condition coefficients, numerical standard errors, and the group-clustered robustness results? Only omnibus creativity findings are printed (PDF pp. 18-19); data are available on reasonable request (PDF p. 23).
notes: Both raw forms were present and parsed. The entire markdown conversion was read, including references and Appendices A-B; relevant facts, statistics, and quotes were checked against extracted PDF text. Page locators are one-based PDF pages, which match the printed pages. The control is other_aid under the codebook rule that includes human partners. The eligible outcome list contains one automated individual creativity-change outcome; neither form supplied a distinct additional eligible outcome. The group outline has no reported creativity score. Discourse transitions, motifs, and agency clusters describe interaction processes; cognitive load, teamwork satisfaction, and psychological safety are self-reports, so these are not eligible creativity/diversity outcomes. The separate human-likeness pilot is not an eligible creative-output study and its people are not added to the main sample: N = 15, M = 5.43, SD = 1.07 on a 7-point Likert scale (PDF p. 9, Section 3.3). In the main manipulation check, AI detection was 25.5% for Supportive-AI and 31.6% for Contrarian-AI (same page and section). Data are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request and are not public because of privacy or ethical restrictions (PDF p. 23, Data Availability); no data or code URL is printed. The three contrast entries identify the study comparisons but repeat the same omnibus evidence, not independent pairwise estimates. No effect size or per-arm people count was calculated. Reconciliation differences count substantive coding or factual-detail differences; equivalent wording, relocation of the same fact across fields, empty synthesis defaults, and reordered open questions are not counted. Missing creativity-analysis Ns and effect statistics are limitations agreed by both screeners, not additional between-form differences. Final review: the full markdown conversion, including references and Appendices A-B, was read; the source version, eligibility evidence, recorded numerical details, and creativity results were checked against PDF text on pp. 1, 7-10, 13, 18-19, 23, and 28-30. The assignment, people, and outcome challenge files all contain empty problems arrays, so challenge_resolution is empty and all challenge-resolution counts are zero. Remaining reporting gaps are classified in final.open_items; the supplement question also covers the sole unresolved reconciliation difference. The reconciliation object is preserved unchanged. This final decision applies to the saved arXiv version; the journal version listed in the search record was not examined.
